{{short description|Right conoid ruled surface}}In [[geometry]], '''Wallis's conical edge''' is a [[ruled surface]] given by the [[parametric equation]]s
: <math>x=v\cos u,\quad y=v\sin u,\quad z=c\sqrt{a^2-b^2\cos^2u}</math>
where {{mvar|a}}, {{mvar|b}} and {{mvar|c}} are constants.

Wallis's conical edge is also a kind of [[right conoid]]. It is named after the English mathematician [[John Wallis]], who was one of the first to use [[Analytic geometry|Cartesian]] methods to study [[conic sections]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=owEj9TMYo7IC&dq=John+Wallis+%22conical+edge%22&pg=PA450|title = Modern Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces with Mathematica, Third Edition|isbn = 9781584884484|last1 = Abbena|first1 = Elsa|last2 = Salamon|first2 = Simon|last3 = Gray|first3 = Alfred|date = 21 June 2006}}</ref>[[Image:Wallis Conical Edge.gif|thumb|400x400px| Figure 2. Wallis's Conical Edge with {{math|1=''a'' = 1.01}}, {{math|1=''b'' = ''c'' = 1}}]][[Image:Wallis's conical edge.svg|thumb|496x496px| Figure 1. Wallis's Conical Edge with {{math|1=''a'' = ''b'' = ''c'' = 1}}|none]]
